summary: Security audit and fixes for input.py

vulnerabilities.description: Unsanitized SQL with string formatting could allow SQL injection.
vulnerabilities.notes: Replaced string formatting with parameterized execute. This prevents user input from changing the SQL structure by sending payloads that would otherwise break out of string context and alter WHERE clauses.

vulnerabilities.description: Unpickling arbitrary user-supplied data leads to remote code execution.
vulnerabilities.fix: Accept JSON instead of pickle for uploaded profiles.
vulnerabilities.notes: Added validation to only accept JSON objects. Rejecting pickled payloads removes the ability for an attacker to send serialized data that executes arbitrary code on deserialization.

vulnerabilities.description: Executing shell with concatenated user input can run arbitrary commands.
vulnerabilities.fix: Whitelisted allowed commands and execute without shell to avoid injection.
vulnerabilities.notes: Added ALLOWED_COMMANDS set and os.spawnlp to run safely. This avoids shell interpretation and limits the server to only run pre-approved commands with explicit arguments.

vulnerabilities.description: User input is rendered into HTML without escaping, enabling XSS.
vulnerabilities.fix: Escape user input using Flask escape helper.
vulnerabilities.notes: greet endpoint now returns escaped name. We use markupsafe escape to convert special HTML characters to entities and prevent injection of script tags.

vulnerabilities.description: Hardcoded API key found in source.
vulnerabilities.fix: Move secrets to environment variables and do not hardcode.
vulnerabilities.notes: API_KEY read from environment now. Avoid committing secrets to source control and use environment variables or secret managers.
